import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 73

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/73](https://www.erdosproblems.com/73)
- [Re99] Reed, B., Mangoes and Blueberries. Combinatorica (1999), 267-296.
-/

namespace Erdos73

/--
Let $k\ge 0$. Let $G$ be a graph such that every subgraph $H$ contains an independent set of size
$\ge (n-k)/2$, where $n$ is the number of vertices of $H$. Must $G$ be the union of a bipartite
graph and $O_k(1)$ many vertices?

Proved by Reed [Re99].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_73 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ (k : ℕ), ∃ (C : ℕ),
      ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
        (∀ (S : Finset V), ∃ (I : Finset V), I ⊆ S ∧ (G.induce (I : Set V)).edgeSet = ∅ ∧
          (I.card : ℝ) ≥ (S.card - k : ℝ) / 2) →
        ∃ (D : Finset V), D.card ≤ C ∧
          (G.induce (D : Set V)ᶜ).Colorable 2 := by
  sorry

-- TODO: Add variants of the problem.

end Erdos73

reformulations.difference: Lean quantifies over finite vertex sets S and requires an edgeless induced graph on I ⊆ S, rather than explicitly quantifying over every subgraph H and requesting an independent set in H.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For any subgraph H with vertex set S, an independent set in G[S] remains independent in H, since deleting edges cannot destroy independence. Conversely, applying the all-subgraphs hypothesis to G[S] supplies exactly the required independent subset of S. The condition (G.induce I).edgeSet = ∅ is equivalent to G.IsIndepSet I. The conclusion uses Colorable 2 on the complement of D, exactly saying G−D is bipartite; C is quantified before the graph and depends only on k. A complete equivalence between these finite-graph statement bodies was proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean without using the admitted Erdős theorem.

sources_consulted: Bruce Reed, Mangoes and Blueberries, Combinatorica 19 (1999), 267–296; publisher preview pp. 267–268, including the conjecture, definition of k-near bipartite, and Remark: https://page-one.springer.com/pdf/preview/10.1007/s004930050056
Local Mathlib sources: Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/Basic.lean, Maps.lean, Subgraph.lean, Clique.lean, Coloring/Vertex.lean, and Bipartite.lean; FormalConjecturesUtil/Answer.lean.
review.notes: Checked the file's sole theorem. Reed's p. 267 formulation matches the Lean claim, and both Reed and the current Erdős database record a positive solution, consistent with answer(True) and research solved. Confirmed that subtraction and division occur in ℝ and that the complement in the conclusion is the vertex-set complement. Scratch proofs cover empty subsets, empty vertex types, edgeless graphs, and k at least the total vertex count; executable tests cover complete graphs through K4 and cycles C4 and C5. The cited https://www.erdosproblems.com/73 page repeatedly returned HTTP 403 despite descriptive User-Agent headers. The mathematical claim and its normalization remark were therefore checked directly in the cited primary paper's publisher preview, with status corroborated by the Erdős database.
